taxonomic_note: Accepted Tragia ramosa Torr.; older treatments vary in synonym and infraspecific placement, so the current Kew/FNA species concept is used.
look_here_first: Look for the branched or scrambling perennial habit, long stinging hairs, narrow toothed leaves, and a small raceme with few male flowers and usually one female flower. Confirm with leaf base, pedicel bases, and fruit.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays is documented by the UT Plant Resources Center Purola Preserve flora; Travis by the UT PRC Euphorbiaceae herbarium index; Bexar by regional vegetation documentation citing TPWD.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Use exact county evidence only; do not infer counties from statewide or ecoregional occurrence.

best_field_traits: perennial subshrub with erect to trailing or scrambling stems
linear-lanceolate to narrowly ovate serrate leaves
leaf bases truncate to weakly cordate
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Narrower leaves with truncate to weakly cordate bases plus the raceme/pedicel characters distinguish it from the local Tragia set; reproductive structures should confirm the ID.
